classification.difficultyReason: Model a box volume, restrict the cutting length and classify the feasible stationary point.

content.prompt: An open rectangular box is made by cutting square corners out of a piece of $60\times60$ cm cardboard and folding up the sides. What is the maximum volume of the box and what are the dimensions of the box?

spec.description: Unlabelled cross-shaped net with four side flaps, removed corner squares and four dashed fold lines around its central square.
spec.mathematics: An open box formed by folding a square sheet after removing four equal corner squares.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question diagram; no answers or dimensions supplied.

answer.short: Maximum volume: $16\,000\text{ cm}^3$. Dimensions: $40\text{ cm}\times40\text{ cm}\times10\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the side length of each removed square. The base is $(60-2x)$ cm by $(60-2x)$ cm and the height is $x$ cm, with $0<x<30$.
$$\begin{aligned}V(x)&=x(60-2x)^2\\V(x)&=4x^3-240x^2+3600x\\V'(x)&=12x^2-480x+3600\\V'(x)&=12(x-10)(x-30).\end{aligned}$$
The only stationary point in the domain is $x=10$.
$$\begin{aligned}V''(x)&=24x-480\\V''(10)&=-240<0\\V(10)&=10(40)^2\\V(10)&=16\,000.\end{aligned}$$
This is the global maximum: it is the only stationary point in the domain, and the volume approaches zero at both ends. The box has dimensions $40\text{ cm}\times40\text{ cm}\times10\text{ cm}$ and maximum volume $16\,000\text{ cm}^3$.
